text:
Priya (Head of Eng): Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands earlier. A few folks asked for clarifications on release cadence, oncall rotations, quality bars, and SLAs — putting an open thread here for follow-ups and concrete next steps.

Jon (VP Eng): Quick summary from my side — goal is predictable 3-week releases for major services, weekly patch windows for critical fixes. Still iterating on what counts as a "major" change.

Maya (Eng Manager): Can we get a short checklist for what needs to land before a release cut? CI green, perf regressions checked, feature flags?

Alex (CTO): Yes — minimal release criteria we discussed: 
- CI: all tests green and flaky test run trimmed; 
- Perf: no >5% regression on 95p latency for core endpoints; 
- Rollout plan: canary + 1 rollback point; 
- Docs: upgrade notes + API changes.

Noah (SRE): For SLAs, ops proposed: 99.9% monthly for hosted API  — we also need SLO error budgets tied to model latency tiers. Will share a PR for numbers.

Priya (Head of Eng): On oncall cadence: there was a request to shorten primary rotation from 3 weeks to 2. Ops impact?

Noah (SRE): 2-week primary is doable but increases handover overhead. Suggest 2-week primary + 1-week follow-on shadow to reduce context loss. Example snippet: 
```
primary: 2w
shadow: 1w
secondary: on-call for weekends (rotating)
```

Maya (Eng Manager): That shadow idea sounds good. Will help with knowledge transfer for teams with frequent context switches.

Jon (VP Eng): Agree. Let's pilot 2w+1w for the next quarter for runtime and api teams. If handovers become noisy, we revert to 3w.

Priya (Head of Eng): Quality bars — a couple of product PMs asked whether we should block release for small model output drift detected by evals. What's the rule?

Alex (CTO): Concrete rule proposal: if automated evals on the golden prompt set show >3% drop in relevance or >5% increase in hallucination rate, block and escalate to model owners. We will tune thresholds per model family.

Maya (Eng Manager): How fast does an owner need to respond to a blocked release? SLAs for that?

Noah (SRE): Recommend 4 business hours acknowledgement for P1 block, 24 hours for P2. We'll include this in the runbook PR.

sre-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary of infra-monitoring v2 at 2026-01-12T14:20:00Z — watch: errors >0.5% trigger rollback.

Priya (Head of Eng): Action items from thread: 
- @Noah: PR with SLO/SLA numbers and oncall pilot plan by EOW.
- @Maya: Draft minimal release checklist and handover template.
- @Alex: Finalize eval thresholds per model family.

Maya (Eng Manager): I'll add a checklist draft to the releases repo and ping folks for feedback.

Jon (VP Eng): Good thread. If anyone else has edge cases (data migrations, infra-only rollouts) drop them here so we can add rules.

Priya (Head of Eng): Thanks — will collect and turn into a short one-page process doc after EOW. :thumbsup:
